vector_db_chunks.text: Section 2(6) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 defines a 'complaint' as an allegation made in writing by a complainant to obtain relief under the Act. Its listed grounds include an unfair contract or an unfair or restrictive trade practice; one or more defects in goods; deficiency in services; charging a price above a price fixed by law, displayed on the goods or package, shown in an exhibited price list, or agreed between the parties; offering hazardous goods or services in circumstances specified by the provision; and a claim for compensation under product-liability provisions. A grievance does not automatically meet this statutory definition or establish entitlement to a remedy; the applicable ground and relief depend on the facts and law.
